title: WHERE A GIGAWATT PAYS LEAST
subtitle: A 1 GW datacenter load, all-in per MWh, at the 14 rows of the All grids tab whose every cost part is held

inputs_words.profile: Datacenter: 0.90 in every hour, never curtails

chart.x_label: Row of the All grids tab (ERCOT)

callouts.label: All-in, USD per MWh, least and most

why: A 1 GW datacenter load, drawing 0.90 of its size in every hour, paid least all-in at ERCOT HB_WEST: USD 40.83 per MWh, USD 321,907,123 a year, and most at ERCOT LZ_CPS: USD 46.69 per MWh, USD 368,100,514 a year. All-in is the day-ahead price over the last twelve whole months, the four-peak transmission charge at the Commission's rate, and capacity, of which ERCOT has none. Only 14 of the tab's 48 rows hold every part: elsewhere transmission is not held, or capacity is held under a license (34 rows). Generators took a median of 45.80 months from request to operation in ERCOT and 100.00 in CAISO, over the requests that came online from 2023 to 2025.
footnote: Data: the All grids tab of "What a datacenter pays" (/cost-of-power?view=allgrids&mw=1000), computed by site/lib/siting.ts from the page's own files: the hourly hub and zone prices (ercot_all_hub_prices_history, ercot_zone_prices_history), ercot_4cp_intervals and the Commission's approved rate (texas_transmission_matrix), and interconnection_durations (Berkeley Lab's Queued Up, 2026 edition (through 2025)). Method: docs/methods/siting.md. The replication: warehouse/replication/siting.py.
source_line: Source: ERW, the All grids tab (/cost-of-power?view=allgrids), from ERCOT's prices and four-peak intervals, the PUCT's transmission matrix and Berkeley Lab's Queued Up (2026 edition (through 2025)).
